newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on primary fall hope.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on primary fall hope.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed 25 basis points down at 22.90 percent, the same rate at which it opened, shadowing expectations that primary rates would fall at Tuesday evening's central bank auction.
"The market opened with expectations of primary rate falls, and trading began on that basis," a trader said.

A Reuters survey of ten secondary money market traders showed they expected the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate to fall by an average of 23 basis points, to 23.23 percent, at the primary auction, and by over 100 basis points on six-month and one-year paper.
In the secondary market, 28-day and 91-day Cetes closed at 23.25 percent and 26.73 percent, respectively, compared to last week's primary rates of 23.46 percent and 27.73 percent.
Traders said that foreign investors were cautious in view of the Fed meeting to review U.S. interest rates due on September 24, and this slowed trade down in the domestic market.

"Trading was sparse, which can be seen that the spread between high and low rates for the day in the overnight market was just 40 basis points," a trader said. "They're waiting to see what will happen with U.S. rates."
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed at 30 basis points down at 24.60 percent.
Earlier, Banco de Mexico injected 5.903 billion pesos by auctioning four credits to offset liquidity shortages, where the lowest assignment rate, at one day, was 24.63 percent.

Total credit maturities for Wednesday will total 8.470 billion pesos, but money returning to the system after the long weekend and planned government spending of 2.8 billion pesos are expected to alleviate ensuing liquidity shortages.
